title: Health and illness
subtitle: a headache, a cold, I feel ill
summary: Say how you feel, name everyday health problems and serious illnesses, and talk about a healthy diet and exercise.

lesson.heading: How are you today?
lesson.text: When someone asks **How are you?** and you are fine, say **I'm very well, thanks** or **I'm fine, thanks**. If you are not fine, you can say how bad the problem is.

examples.text: I **don't feel very well**. I must go home and rest.
I **feel ill**. Can you get a doctor, please?
That fish was bad. I think I'm going to **be sick**!

lesson.heading: Everyday problems
lesson.text: Small problems come and go. You say **I've got a headache** when your head hurts, **I've got toothache** when a tooth hurts, and **I've got a cold** when your nose is red and you sneeze.

examples.text: Have you got an aspirin? I've got a **headache**.
I've got **toothache**. I need to go to the dentist.
I'm going to bed with a hot drink. I've got **a cold**.

lesson.heading: Problem and what you do
rows: go to bed with a hot drink

lesson.heading: Problems people have for many years
lesson.text: Some problems stay with people all their lives. **Hay fever** comes from flowers and grass in summer and makes you **sneeze**. If you have **asthma**, sometimes you can't **breathe**.

examples.text: I get **hay fever** every summer. I **sneeze** all day.
My little brother has **asthma**; sometimes he can't breathe.
Pollution and traffic fumes are bad for people with **asthma**.

lesson.heading: Illnesses in hot countries
lesson.text: In some hot countries, mosquitoes give people **malaria**. Bad drinking water can give people **cholera**.

examples.text: In some countries, mosquitoes can give people **malaria**.
The drinking water was bad, and many children had **cholera**.

lesson.heading: Serious illnesses
lesson.text: **Cancer** and a **heart attack** are serious. Note that people **have** a heart attack.

examples.text: Every year **cancer** kills many people who smoke.
My father went to hospital when he **had a heart attack**.

lesson.heading: Staying healthy
lesson.text: A **healthy diet** is lots of fruit and vegetables. **Exercise** like swimming, jogging and cycling is good for you. When you feel **stressed**, you need to **relax** more.

examples.text: *A:* Do you have a **healthy diet**? *B:* Yes, I eat lots of fruit and vegetables.
*A:* Do you **exercise**? *B:* Yes, I like swimming, jogging and cycling.
*A:* I feel **stressed**! *B:* You need to **relax** more and don't panic about work!

lesson.text: Remember the verb: my father **had** a heart attack - not ~~got a heart attack~~.

exercises.prompt: *A:* How are you today? *B:* Very ___, thanks.
exercises.explanation: I'm very well, thanks = I feel fine.

exercises.prompt: Have you got an aspirin? I've got a ___.
exercises.explanation: When your head hurts, you have a headache.

exercises.prompt: I've got ___. I need to go to the dentist.
exercises.explanation: We say I've got toothache, without a.

exercises.prompt: Your nose is red and you are sneezing. What have you got?
exercises.explanation: With a cold you go to bed with a hot drink.

exercises.prompt: Match each illness with the thing that causes it.
That fish was bad. I think I'm going to be ___!
My father went to hospital when he ___ a heart attack.
exercises.explanation: People have a heart attack, not get one.

exercises.statement: My grandfather got a heart attack last year.
exercises.explanation: My grandfather had a heart attack last year. Use have, not get, with heart attack.

exercises.prompt: Is it a small everyday problem or a serious illness?
I get hay fever every summer. I ___ all day.
exercises.explanation: Hay fever comes from flowers and grass and makes you sneeze.

exercises.prompt: You feel very ill. Ask for help.
exercises.answer: Can you get a doctor, please?

exercises.prompt: *A:* Do you have a healthy ___? *B:* Yes, I eat lots of fruit and vegetables.
exercises.explanation: Your diet is the food you eat.

exercises.statement: I feel stressed, so I need to relax more and not panic about work.
exercises.explanation: Correct. When you feel stressed you need to relax.
